+    private val onToggleListViewModeClicked: () -> Unit,

+    override fun getLayout(): Int = R.layout.subscription_groups_header

+    override fun bind(
+        viewBinding: SubscriptionGroupsHeaderBinding,
+        position: Int,
+        payloads: MutableList<Any>
+    ) {
+        if (payloads.contains(PAYLOAD_UPDATE_ICONS)) {
+            updateIcons(viewBinding)
+            return
+        }
+
+        super.bind(viewBinding, position, payloads)
+    }
+
+    override fun bind(viewBinding: SubscriptionGroupsHeaderBinding, position: Int) {
+        viewBinding.headerTitle.text = title
+        viewBinding.headerSort.setOnClickListener { onSortClicked() }

+    }
+
+    override fun initializeViewBinding(view: View) = SubscriptionGroupsHeaderBinding.bind(view)
+

+        viewBinding.headerToggleViewMode.setImageResource(
+            if (listViewMode) R.drawable.ic_apps else R.drawable.ic_list
+        )

I don't think this is needed, using the `Toast` methods by themselves in classes which need them ensures that you apply the duration show you wanted.

This is a personal opinion, though.
You must create a string ressource and reference it here, to allow translation of this message.

As you can see on [the JavaDoc of the error code](https://exoplayer.dev/doc/reference/com/google/android/exoplayer2/PlaybackException.html#ERROR_CODE_IO_NETWORK_CONNECTION_FAILED), using this error and show to the user that it doesn't have a connection in this case is not appropriate for all cases.

I recommend checking the network connection using the system APIs / compat/JetPack APIs if there are ones instead.
